## Context

Mutation testing should protect changed behavioral cores, but the historical whole-file counts are stale. A pinned mutmut 3.7.0 probe found 814 mutants in `signing.py` versus 491 in the old record, including both equivalent survivors and real contract gaps. Enforcing the old ceilings would block unrelated work; accepting all current survivors would normalize defects. The approved rollout therefore starts with evidence gathering and promotes each shard only when its results and runtime justify stronger enforcement.

## Plan

Use `.github/mutation-shards.toml` as the sole source for shard mappings, reviewed equivalent fingerprints, and an explicit per-shard enforcement mode:

- `advisory`: run head mutation evidence, publish every outcome, and do not fail Gerrit for mutation-quality findings. Configuration, selection, execution, and artifact-contract failures still fail because usable evidence was not produced.
- `ratchet`: compare fresh base/head archives. For AST-identical functions, preserve unchanged legacy survivors and `no tests` outcomes. Block killed mutants that disappear or become survived, timed out, incomplete, or `no tests`; block new survivors, timeouts, and incomplete statuses. Report newly introduced `no tests` without blocking because mutmut cannot reliably attribute subprocess tests. Added or edited functions must kill every mutant unless a survivor matches an individually reviewed equivalent fingerprint.
- `strict`: apply the changed-function rule to the entire shard. Every mutant must be killed or individually fingerprinted as equivalent; `no tests`, timeouts, incomplete statuses, and zero mutants block. Strict promotion therefore requires direct in-process mutation coverage.

Start all legacy shards as advisory. Promote a shard to ratchet only after three successful base/head pilot runs show stable mappings and a maximum runtime of 24 minutes or less inside its 30-minute job. If a shard cannot meet that threshold, narrow it to proven function patterns before promotion. Promote it to strict only after legacy non-killed outcomes are remediated or individually reviewed. Mode changes are small manifest reviews; there is no fuzzy severity classification.

A selector inspects `HEAD^..HEAD`, including both sides of renames. Mapped source, test, or support changes select their shards; mutation-infrastructure changes select all. Unmapped changed Python tests are reported as advisory findings. Unresolved refs or diffs fail; an empty selection is an explicit successful skip. The reusable workflow emits selector JSON and creates one matrix job per selected shard, so every shard has its own 30-minute cap. Advisory evaluates head only; ratchet evaluates fresh base and head archives; strict evaluates complete head evidence plus the regression evidence required by the driver.

For each archive the driver synthesizes `[tool.mutmut]` from the canonical manifest before execution. The repository does not retain a second global `[tool.mutmut]` shard mapping. Each job uses Python 3.12, pinned `mutmut==3.7.0`, `--max-children 1`, configured per-mutant timeout behavior, and selected clean-test preflight. Dependency downloads may be cached; mutation verdict state may not. Gerrit checks out the exact patchset and includes mutation in `vote.needs`; the push/PR lane mirrors it. A weekly/manual sweep selects every shard through the same selector and matrix.

Mutation-result reruns are diagnostic only and cannot turn red green. Only independently identified setup failures may retry. Raw logs, survivor diffs and fingerprints, and a structured summary publish for every driver outcome. Documentation describes the live manifest policy and promotion process and removes stale score or budget tables. The existing two-vote rollback runbook remains the emergency recovery path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selection tests cover source, test, support, and global inputs; renames and deletions; unmatched tests; empty selection; unresolved refs; selector JSON; and all-shard selection.
- [ ] Manifest tests cover explicit modes, invalid modes, generated per-archive mutmut configuration, and removal of duplicate repository configuration.
- [ ] Advisory tests prove mutation-quality findings are reported but do not fail, while missing evidence and configuration or execution failures still fail.
- [ ] Ratchet tests prove unchanged legacy survivors and `no tests` are grandfathered; newly introduced `no tests` is reported without blocking; and killed regressions, missing killed mutants, new survivors, timeouts, and incomplete statuses block.
- [ ] Ratchet tests prove added or edited functions require killed mutants or individually reviewed equivalent fingerprints.
- [ ] Strict tests prove the whole shard meets the clean rule and every `no tests` outcome blocks.
- [ ] Execution tests prove fresh archives, no verdict-cache restore, pinned runtime and concurrency, clean-test preflight, generated configuration, structured artifacts, and zero-mutant detection.
- [ ] Workflow tests prove selector-derived per-shard matrix jobs, a 30-minute limit for each shard, exact Gerrit patchset checkout, `vote.needs`, push/PR parity, weekly/manual all-shard selection, cancellation, and always-published artifacts.
- [ ] A real compact-policy smoke run passes from fresh base/head archives.
- [ ] Documentation explains the phased modes, deterministic promotion evidence, false-positive policy, cadence, and manifest authority without stale score or budget tables.

## Verification

    pytest -q tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py
    python scripts/mutation_gate.py smoke --shard compact-policy --base HEAD^ --head HEAD
    python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py
    make config-check
    make lint
    make typecheck

## Primary evidence

Current primary-source examples: Instructor uses a pinned bounded shard with explicit exceptions; DataDog maps changed tests to source and compares base/head; PostHog gates a targeted PR shard; Trailmark cancels superseded runs and always reports; GeoParquet schedules broad mutation, fails on missing evidence, retries setup only, and publishes artifacts. The real pinned-tool probe and corrections are recorded in concise ticket comments.
